descripcion: Estima la clase de hemorragia aguda del adulto con trauma (I a IV) y la pérdida aproximada de volemia a partir de los signos clínicos y el déficit de base, según la tabla 3-1 y el capítulo de choque del ATLS 10.ª edición. Manda el peor parámetro: orienta la reanimación inicial, que después se ajusta a la respuesta.
instrucciones: Marcar cada signo tal como está ahora. Manda el parámetro que indica la clase más alta. No esperar a que el paciente encaje en una clase para reanimar.
limitaciones: Los signos son un continuo y sólo guían el tratamiento inicial. El anciano, el atleta, el niño, el embarazo y los betabloqueadores cambian la respuesta: una PAS de 100 mmHg puede ser choque en el anciano. No sirve para el choque que no es hemorrágico.

elementos.label: Frecuencia cardíaca
elementos.ayuda: Los betabloqueadores y el buen estado físico del atleta pueden esconder la taquicardia.

elementos.label: Presión arterial sistólica
elementos.ayuda: Cae de forma constante desde la clase III (pérdida de más del 30 %).

elementos.label: Presión de pulso

opciones.label: Muy estrecha o diastólica que no se mide

elementos.ayuda: Se estrecha antes de que caiga la sistólica: mírala en la clase II.

elementos.label: Déficit de base

opciones.label: Sin gases o de 0 a −2 mEq/L

elementos.ayuda: Es el exceso de base negativo de los gases arteriales.

resultados.approach: Es un evento **preterminal**: activar el **protocolo de transfusión masiva** y controlar el sangrado con cirugía inmediata.
Detener el sangrado con cirugía o **embolización** y transfundir **glóbulos rojos** y hemoderivados.
Reanimar con **cristaloide** y buscar la fuente; algunos necesitarán **transfusión**.
Signos **mínimos**: en el sano no suele hacer falta reponer. Vigilar y **reevaluar**: el sangrado puede seguir.

referencias.texto: For otherwise healthy patients, this amount of blood loss does not require replacement, because transcapillary refill and other compensatory mechanisms will restore blood volume within 24 hours

referencias.texto: Clinical signs of class II hemorrhage include tachycardia, tachypnea, and decreased pulse pressure

referencias.titulo: American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma. Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS): Student Course Manual. 10th ed. Chicago: American College of Surgeons; 2018. (Cap. 3: diuresis en la clase II)
referencias.texto: The measured urine flow is usually 20 to 30 mL/hour in an adult with class II hemorrhage

referencias.titulo: American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma. Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS): Student Course Manual. 10th ed. Chicago: American College of Surgeons; 2018. (Cap. 3: la clase II se estabiliza con cristaloide)
referencias.texto: Some patients in this category may eventually require blood transfusion, but most are stabilized initially with crystalloid solutions

referencias.titulo: American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma. Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS): Student Course Manual. 10th ed. Chicago: American College of Surgeons; 2018. (Cap. 3: signos de la clase III)
referencias.texto: Patients with class III hemorrhage typically present with the classic signs of inadequate perfusion, including marked tachycardia and tachypnea, significant changes in mental status, and a measurable fall in systolic blood pressure

referencias.titulo: American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma. Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS): Student Course Manual. 10th ed. Chicago: American College of Surgeons; 2018. (Cap. 3: clase III, la PAS cae)
referencias.texto: In an uncomplicated case, this is the least amount of blood loss that consistently causes a drop in systolic blood pressure

referencias.titulo: American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma. Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS): Student Course Manual. 10th ed. Chicago: American College of Surgeons; 2018. (Cap. 3: tratamiento de la clase III)
referencias.texto: The priority of initial management is to stop the hemorrhage, by emergency operation or embolization, if necessary. Most patients in this category will require packed red blood cells (pRBCs) and blood products

referencias.titulo: American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma. Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS): Student Course Manual. 10th ed. Chicago: American College of Surgeons; 2018. (Cap. 3: signos de la clase IV)
referencias.texto: Symptoms include marked tachycardia, a significant decrease in systolic blood pressure, and a very narrow pulse pressure or unmeasurable diastolic blood pressure

referencias.titulo: American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma. Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS): Student Course Manual. 10th ed. Chicago: American College of Surgeons; 2018. (Cap. 3: diuresis y conciencia en la clase IV)
referencias.texto: Urinary output is negligible, and mental status is markedly depressed. The skin is cold and pale

referencias.titulo: American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma. Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS): Student Course Manual. 10th ed. Chicago: American College of Surgeons; 2018. (Cap. 3: tratamiento de la clase IV)
referencias.texto: Patients with class IV hemorrhage frequently require rapid transfusion and immediate surgical intervention

referencias.titulo: American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma. Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS): Student Course Manual. 10th ed. Chicago: American College of Surgeons; 2018. (Cap. 3: transfusión masiva)
referencias.texto: massive transfusion, most often defined as > 10 units of pRBCs within the first 24 hours of admission or more than 4 units in 1 hour

referencias.titulo: American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma. Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS): Student Course Manual. 10th ed. Chicago: American College of Surgeons; 2018. (Cap. 3: no esperar a una clase precisa)
referencias.texto: It is dangerous to wait until a trauma patient fits a precise physiologic classification of shock before initiating appropriate volume restoration

referencias.titulo: American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma. Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS): Student Course Manual. 10th ed. Chicago: American College of Surgeons; 2018. (Cap. 3: no basta un solo parámetro)
referencias.texto: Diagnosis of shock can be missed when only a single parameter is used. • Use all clinical information, including heart rate, blood pressure, skin perfusion, and mental status

referencias.titulo: American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma. Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS): Student Course Manual. 10th ed. Chicago: American College of Surgeons; 2018. (Cap. 3: PAS de 100 en el anciano)
referencias.texto: For example, a systolic blood pressure of 100 mm Hg may represent shock in an elderly patient

referencias.texto: ß-adrenergic blockade can mask tachycardia as an early indicator of shock
